title: ALMA observations of 4U 1728-34 and 4U 1820-30: first detection of neutron star X-ray binaries at 300 GHz
question: How do jet properties (radio-to-mm spectrum and the optically thick/thin break) of two atoll neutron-star X-ray binaries relate to their hard/soft states, compared with black holes?

what.value: Deep ATCA 6 km-configuration model of NGC 6624 used to subtract compact sources

evidence.quote: We therefore used a model made from deep images of NGC 6624 at the same observing frequencies (Tudor et al., in prep.)

what.value: Hard/soft-state 15-50 keV flux thresholds from previous broad-band X-ray observations

evidence.quote: we calculated the 15–50 keV fluxes typical of hard and soft states based on previous observations of the source with broad-band X-ray detectors

recipe.goal: Image ALMA continuum and measure flux
recipe.method: Re-generate images from calibrated products, self-calibrate, primary-beam correct, fit elliptical Gaussian for peak flux
Compare Swift/BAT 15-50 keV fluxes with typical hard/soft thresholds (1e-9 erg/cm2/s) and hardness ratio
assumptions: power-law index 1 or 2 for BAT count-to-flux conversion

recipe.goal: Fit radio-to-IR SED spectral indices and jet break
recipe.method: Power-law fits F_nu ∝ nu^alpha to ATCA+ALMA(+IR) points; break from interpolation of thick and thin spectra

recipe.goal: Identify nature of additional ALMA sources
recipe.method: HST counterpart search, isochrone masses (Dartmouth), chance-coincidence and background-source counts

evidence.quote: we obtain $\alpha$ = 0.28 $\pm$ 0.05 and a spectral break at $\sim$6 $(\pm$ 5)$\times$10$^{13}$ Hz
we obtain a spectral slope of 0.13 $\pm$ 0.04
with a flux density of $236\pm27$ $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$
